theory.intro: A length can be written in two ways: as a whole number of small units, or as a decimal of larger units. For example $165$ cm $= 1.65$ m.
facts: There are $100$ cm in $1$ m, so each centimetre is $\tfrac{1}{100}$ of a metre ($0.01$ m).
There are $1000$ mm in $1$ m and $10$ mm in $1$ cm.
Place value carries the meaning: $1.65$ m is $1$ whole metre and $65$ hundredths of a metre.
steps: Decide which units are used and how many smaller units make one larger unit: $100$ cm $=1$ m, $1000$ mm $=1$ m, or $10$ mm $=1$ cm.
To write a decimal length, separate any whole larger units, then use decimal place value for the remaining smaller units. Keep zeros in empty places.

To read a decimal length, keep the whole-unit part and read the decimal places in smaller units. In metres, hundredths are centimetres and thousandths are millimetres; in centimetres, tenths are millimetres.

workedExamples.question_text:
Record each length using decimal notation.
(a) $283$ cm in metres
(b) $76$ mm in centimetres
(c) $13$ mm in metres
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $283\text{ cm}=2\text{ m }83\text{ cm}$.
$83\text{ cm}$ is $83$ hundredths of a metre.
$283\text{ cm}=2.83\text{ m}$.
(b) $76\text{ mm}=7\text{ cm }6\text{ mm}$.
$6\text{ mm}$ is $6$ tenths of a centimetre.
$76\text{ mm}=7.6\text{ cm}$.
(c) $13\text{ mm}$ is $13$ thousandths of a metre.
Write the thousandths using three digits: $013$.
$13\text{ mm}=0.013\text{ m}$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Interpret these decimal lengths using the stated units.
(a) $4.036$ m in metres, centimetres and millimetres
(b) $8.7$ cm in centimetres and millimetres
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $4.036\text{ m}=4\text{ m}+0.036\text{ m}$.
$0.036\text{ m}=36\text{ mm}=3\text{ cm }6\text{ mm}$.
The length is $4\text{ m }3\text{ cm }6\text{ mm}$.
(b) $8.7\text{ cm}=8\text{ cm}+0.7\text{ cm}$.
$0.7\text{ cm}=7\text{ mm}$.
The length is $8\text{ cm }7\text{ mm}$.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) A student writes $5$ m $7$ cm as $5.7$ m. Explain the error and give the correct decimal length.
(b) Complete the missing digit: $4.0\square9$ m $=4$ m $8$ cm $9$ mm.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $7\text{ cm}=0.07\text{ m}$, because centimetres are hundredths of a metre.
$5.7\text{ m}$ means $5\text{ m }70\text{ cm}$.
The correct length is $5.07\text{ m}$.
(b) $8\text{ cm }9\text{ mm}=89\text{ mm}=0.089\text{ m}$.
$4\text{ m }8\text{ cm }9\text{ mm}=4.089\text{ m}$.
The missing digit is $8$.

foundation.question_text: Record $142$ cm as a decimal number of metres.
Interpret $3.27$ m as metres and centimetres.
Record $68$ mm as a decimal number of centimetres.
Interpret $14.6$ cm as centimetres and millimetres.
Write $5$ m $34$ cm using metres in decimal notation.
Which decimal length in metres is equivalent to $209$ cm?

development.question_text: Record $7$ cm as a decimal number of metres.
Record $9$ mm as a decimal number of metres.
Interpret $12.05$ m as metres and centimetres.
Interpret $0.7$ cm as a whole number of millimetres.
development.solution_text:
$0.7\text{ cm}=7$ tenths of a centimetre
$=7\text{ mm}$

development.question_text: Write $8$ m $4$ cm using metres in decimal notation.
Complete the equivalence: $3.\square5$ m $=3$ m $45$ cm.

mastery.question_text: Noah writes $6$ m $8$ cm as $6.8$ m. Explain his place-value error and give the correct decimal length.
mastery.solution_text:
$8\text{ cm}$ is $8$ hundredths of a metre, not $8$ tenths.
$6\text{ m }8\text{ cm}=6.08\text{ m}$

mastery.question_text:
A ribbon is $2.045$ m long.
Record its length using metres, centimetres and millimetres.
mastery.solution_text:
$0.045\text{ m}=45\text{ mm}$
$45\text{ mm}=4\text{ cm }5\text{ mm}$
$2.045\text{ m}=2\text{ m }4\text{ cm }5\text{ mm}$

mastery.question_text:
A length is written as $4.0a7$ m. It is also $4$ m $6$ cm $7$ mm.
Find the digit $a$.
mastery.solution_text:
$6\text{ cm }7\text{ mm}=67\text{ mm}=0.067\text{ m}$
$4\text{ m }6\text{ cm }7\text{ mm}=4.067\text{ m}$
$a=6$
